examples.text: Je songeai que si j’adoptais durablement ce style de vie, je ne tarderais pas à devenir le gros chat préfiguré par Biscuit.
Le paranoïaque écoute l’autre d’une manière différente, distord la phrase, préfigure le sens, y découvre ce qu’il cherchait, à savoir qu’on l’accuse, lui, des fautes que l’accusateur a commises.

glosses: To show or suggest ahead of time; to represent beforehand.

examples.text: Hong Kong, Singapore and Shanghai, all prefigure NRx urban futures.

glosses: That which prefigures or appears to predict; a harbinger.

examples.text: Quite different is the way in which the tomboy girled the rebel narrative. In recent years, queer theorists have taken a deep interest in the tomboy as a prefigure for the butch dyke.
In his influential commentary (the Moralia) Gregory the Great interpreted the protagonist typologically as a prefigure of Christ and of the Church persecuted.

glosses: To presage, or suggest something in advance.

examples.text: It all sounds to us remarkably nineteenth-century; Petrarch's romantic sentiments foreshadow with uncanny precision those of Dante Gabriel Rossetti or Alfred de Musset.
If there is a significant or surprising event in the story, it must be foreshadowed earlier on. When the event that was foreshadowed occurs, that's the payoff.
